issue.title: Should I expect completion of nested command's flags to work?
issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/urfave/cli/discussions/1915
Originally posted by **ldelossa** May 25, 2024 Hello, I have a root command called 'cmd'. Now I have a sub command hanging off this called "sub-command". The cli.Command for "sub-command" defines 2 flags "--a, --b". All commands have the "EnableShellCompletion" boolean set to true. I'm using `zsh`. Should I expect to see completion for `cmd subcommand --`. My assumption was to see completion for `--a, --b` but instead the only completion I get is for `--h, -help` essentially.

comments.author: dearchap
comments.body: @ldelossa Its okay to generate the cmd graph from a yaml. I dont see any real issues with your implementation. It should work. You sourced the zsh completion script for this app correct ? Everytime you hit <tab> on the terminal for completion(for this app) the app will be run with the --generate-shell-completion arg so that the app can output the cmd/flags as needed. Have you tried putting this through a debugger to see whats going on ?

comments.author: dearchap
comments.body:
@ldelossa I tried out your lean code and it works for me. Are you in a zsh first of all ? also how are you invoking the program ```main``` or ```./main``` . For me ```main``` is throwing some vague output whereas ```./main``` works just fine with tab completion

```
% echo $ZSH_NAME
zsh
% echo $ZSH_VERSION
5.8
```

comments.author: dearchap
comments.body: Are you hitting TAB after the command and you see the subcommand ? If you hit the TAB after subcommand you should see h for help. The generate-shell-completion arg is automatically passed to the program when TAB is hit. You shouldn't need to type in --generate-shell-completion manually unless you are testing the autocomplete behavior . So what exactly is the problem here ? I'm confused
